title: picard_residue_homology_source_residue_comparison
statement:
Under the complete signature below, the explicit degree-one affine residue cycles modulo boundaries compute the derived residue fibre of any object represented by the strictly perfect complex; no geometric direct-image data are assumed.

Exact Lean statement:
theorem picard_residue_homology_source_residue_comparison
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{v},
      HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1} (SheafOfModules.{v} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ (Y : Scheme.{v}) (U : Y.Opens), HasDerivedCategory.{v + 1}
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace).over U))]
    (W : Scheme.{v}) (E : schemeDerivedCategory W) (w : W)
    (U : W.Opens) (hwU : w ∈ U) (hU : IsAffineOpen U)
    (p : Ideal Γ(W, U)) [p.IsPrime]
    (hp : p = RingHom.ker (W.evaluation U w hwU).hom)
    (K : CochainComplex
      (SheafOfModules.{v} ((moduleRings W.toRingedSpace).over U)) ℤ)
    (hK : IsStrictlyPerfect W U K)
    (hE : Nonempty ((SheafOfModules.overFunctor.{v}
      (moduleRings W.toRingedSpace) U).mapDerivedCategory.obj E ≅
        DerivedCategory.Q.obj K)) :
    Nonempty (affineResidueCycleHomology W U p K ≃+
      derivedFiberCohomology W E 1 w)

source.place: Tags 01IB, 064K, 06YJ and 010V; affine projective retractions and module homology

proof.text: Apply the source model theorem to identify derived fibre cohomology with degree-one homology of the scalar-extended section complex, and apply the quotient model theorem to identify the explicit affine residue quotient with the same homology. Compose the resulting additive equivalences.
